title: Erdős 249 gcd-moment calculus: half-geometric normalizations and dyadic positivity

concepts.label: half-geometric Mersenne normalization
concepts.note: At r=1/2, the Lambert factor r^d/(1-r^d) is exactly 1/(2^d-1), including its square.

concepts.label: shifted geometric tail
concepts.note: The positive-index geometric sum has the closed form x/(1-x).

concepts.label: positive dyadic denominators
concepts.note: Every positive natural exponent gives 2^a at least two.

concepts.label: normalization-toolkit boundary
concepts.note: These classical identities license exact series rewrites and positivity checks; they do not prove the gcd-moment evaluations or any irrationality claim by themselves.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: PROVED NORMALIZATION TOOLKIT: for every positive d, ((1/2)^d)/(1-(1/2)^d)=1/(2^d-1), and squaring gives the corresponding reciprocal-square identity. More generally, for 0≤x<1, the sum over g≥0 of x^(g+1) is x/(1-x).
statement_nodes.engine: Clear the positive dyadic denominators algebraically and factor one power of x from the classical geometric series.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Standard geometric-series algebra and its specialization at one half.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The identities rewrite individual factors and one elementary sum. They do not justify unrelated sum exchanges, establish q-Padé irrationality, or evaluate the full gcd-moment series without the separate landed theorems that consume them.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: PROVED DYADIC LOWER BOUND: for every positive natural a, 2≤2^a; in particular 2^a-1 is positive, as required by the cylinder-mass denominator arguments.
statement_nodes.engine: Monotonicity of powers of two from exponent one to a positive exponent.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: This is only the positivity side condition for later rational cylinder identities; it contains no asymptotic or arithmetic information.

intra_zone_relations.basis: The dyadic lower bound supplies the denominator positivity used by the half-geometric reciprocal-Mersenne normalization.
